analysis:
Both units are the same test-only file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Config/ClusterRuntimeApprovalFactsTests.swift. The patch expands ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts tests and the test Fixture, with no production code and no change to a runtime control. The changes cover: pair-serving grants and their evidence digests; declared public-model qualifications and pipeline cuts derived from config.json num_hidden_layers; release-candidate selection that reads catalog.json; handling of catalog IDs that name another registered model; and release model derivation from passing records.

The tests exercise fail-closed behavior. Examples: a contradicting divergence record removes a grant; a catalog entry that isn't the candidate's own is refused; and a release with no qualified model is refused. These match the intent of A-017 and TB-011 (qualification evidence and fail-closed grants). The fixtures only use temporary directories and a shell stand-in for the worker, and they create no real keys or secrets. The metadataFixtures path refactor only locates repo fixtures and has no security effect.

The patch excerpt was truncated, and the new cluster API behavior (ClusterPublicModels, ClusterPairServingGrants, the release function) is not shown in source. I could not check that production code enforces what these tests assert. That belongs to a review of the production source, not to this test-only change, and does not indicate a regression here. No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumption was identified in these units.
